A tool earns "monthly" only if some rule family produced valid findings that were worth acting on. Precision alone kept jscpd in the list for two runs it should not have been in.

THE CONTROL THAT CHANGED HOW TO READ EVERY RATE
13 of 20 rows flipped verdict when the tool and rule names were removed — including 3 validity calls.
Same model, same rows, same code. So the pilot's 20-of-49 split along rule families was substantially the brand, not
the code. Consequence: per-family validity counts from one adjudicator are usable; per-family actionability and
consequence are one opinion; and no unblinded per-family rate may be quoted as a precision measurement.
